key_insight: The paper shows that making logic-gate and LUT connections trainable, not just the gate/LUT values, yields more accurate and far more compact deep discrete networks.
engineering_relevance: This enables hardware-friendly neural models with fewer gates and trainable wiring, which is attractive for efficient edge AI and digital logic implementation.
method: Use a probability distribution over possible input connections for each gate/LUT pin.
Select the highest-merit connection while training gate types or LUT entries in parallel.
Stabilize deep training with high learning rates, straight-through estimators, and removal of constant-output gate types.
evidence_signal: On MNIST, the method reaches 98.92% with two layers of 8000 gates and 98.45% with one layer, while LUTNs achieve 98.88% with two layers of 2000 6-input LUTs.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful training stability tricks, so the method may be sensitive to hyperparameters and implementation details in deeper networks.
paper_title: Fully Trainable Deep Differentiable Logic Gate Networks and Lookup Table Networks
